blocks.content: Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of citizens of India. They are defined in Part IVA of the Constitution under Article 51A. These duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
1. Background of Fundamental Duties

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution via the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, following the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
Originally 10 duties were added under Article 51A; the 11th duty was later added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002.
Fundamental Duties apply strictly to citizens of India and do not extend to foreign nationals.
Like the Directive Principles of State Policy, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and cannot be directly enforced through courts without specific legislative sanction.

blocks.content: • Originally, the Constitution did not contain Fundamental Duties.
• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976.
• The idea was borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
• Later, the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002) added one more duty.
2. Article 51A – List of Fundamental Duties

cells: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
To cherish and follow the noble ideals of the freedom struggle
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To defend the country and render national service when called upon
To promote harmony and brotherhood among all people of India
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife
To develop scientific temper, humanism and spirit of inquiry
To safeguard public property and avoid violence
To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
Duty of parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to children between 6 and 14 years

blocks.content: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
3. Features of Fundamental Duties
• They are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).
• They apply only to citizens of India.
• They act as a moral responsibility of citizens.
• They help promote discipline and unity in society.

rows: Applies to Citizens and Foreigners (select rights)
Applies exclusively to Citizens of India

blocks.content: 4. Importance of Fundamental Duties
• Promote patriotism and national unity.
• Encourage citizens to protect the environment and public property.
• Help maintain discipline in society.
• Complement Fundamental Rights.
5. Difference between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties

items: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended 8 duties, but the 42nd Amendment Act added 10 duties in 1976.
The 11th Fundamental Duty regarding education for children aged 6 to 14 years was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the constitution of the former USSR.
Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, but Parliament can enact legislation to enforce compliance and impose penalties.

blocks.content: SSC / SSC Exam Important Facts
• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976).
• They are contained in Article 51A.
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties.
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Soviet Constitution.
